content.title: March Miracle Dukes Caleb Foster goes from surgery to savior in 19 days
content.text: The junior guard scored 11 points in the second half to lead the Blue Devils to an 80-75 win over St. John's less than three weeks after having surgery on his right foot. WASHINGTON, D.C. — Jon Scheyer cried, Duke's head trainer proclaimed a miracle and Caleb Foster etched himself into Blue Devils lore on Friday night at Capital One Arena. After saving their season in the Sweet 16 against relentless Big East champion St. John's, Foster wheeled himself from Duke's locker room to the interview room on the same scooter that has gotten him around for the last three weeks. "Still a little stunned with what happened," said a glassy-eyed Scheyer. "Because what this guy did, to be honest, he had no business playing tonight. Ninety-nine percent of guys do not come back to play under the circumstances of what happened to him. It was incredible the way he willed us. There's no analytics, there's no stats that can measure how big this dude's heart is for what he did." What he did: After Rick Pitino's team pressed and pummeled and poured in 3-pointers, when the Red Storm had blown away Duke with a 15-1 run to take a 55-45 lead in the second half of their East Regional semifinal, Foster took over. Three straight drives into the paint, three straight buckets, then a drawn foul on the fourth. He scored seven consecutive points to steady the Blue Devils.Then, with 2:14 to go and protecting a four-point lead, Foster sidestepped a defender and drilled a jumper. With 1:27 to go and the lead down to three, Foster drove, hung and sank a contested layup for what proved to be the decisive bucket in an 80-75 win that sent the Blue Devils to their third consecutive Elite Eight. "Miracles happen in March," Blue Devils head trainer Jose Fonseca said. "I think we just witnessed the first one for us." Twenty days earlier, in the regular-season finale, Foster planted his right foot awkwardly in the first half of a win over North Carolina. Nineteen days earlier, Foster had surgery on that foot. If the injury had happened in the summer or fall, Fonseca said, he would've told Scheyer to count on a six- to eight-week recovery timeline.
